speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a neonate presenting with seizures, lethargy, and neurological signs three days after birth. To begin my assessment, please tell me if your mother had any complications during delivery, such as prolonged rupture of membranes or a fever?

speaker: Patient
text: 1100-g (2-lb 7-oz) newborn, 31 weeks' gestation. The patient was born three days ago with a birth weight of 1100 g at 31 weeks' gestation. The antenatal period was complicated by chorioamnionitis. Apgar scores were 3 and 6 at 1 and 5 minutes, respectively. The patient has become increasingly lethargic over the past 18 hours and experienced a tonic seizure lasting for 25 seconds.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The history of chorioamnionitis and low birth weight raises concern for an infectious cause. Given the seizures and lethargy, I need to evaluate your metabolic and inflammatory status immediately.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Sepsis (likely Group B Streptococcus or E. coli) with possible Hypocalcemia or Hypoglycemia.

REQUEST TEST: CBC, Blood Culture, Blood Glucose, Calcium, Magnesium, Procalcitonin, CRP, and CSF Analysis.
REQUEST IMAGES: Lumbar_Puncture_Fluoroscopy, Head_Ultrasound.
